context_documents.title: 2022-179 · Break symmetric jams and choose a reliable climb pace
context_documents.body:
# 2022-179: Break symmetric jams and choose a reliable climb pace

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Foam collector contacts replace earlier rubber/mecanum choices; agitation addresses two-cargo jams. The retained account describes staged wrong-color ejection, a powered upper roller added after South Florida and a hooded turret. The team reports a roughly ten-second traversal with faster but less reliable trials.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source explicitly prefers the slightly slower climb because faster operation sometimes behaves unpredictably.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A peak mechanism time should not replace a completion-probability model. In transport, a symmetric two-ball load can remain jammed unless agitation changes relative contact, even when a single ball flows easily.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure full-cycle jam rate, rejection interactions and climb success versus timing, not only best-case speed.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/g9lcyx_c5ig](https://youtu.be/g9lcyx_c5ig)

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with Children of the Swamp at Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:30–4:25 pickup and agitator; 4:28–6:04 sensing/indexer; 6:06–7:31 shooter; 7:34–9:08 climb
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: Foam contacts replaced earlier rubber and mecanum variants, and a rotating agitator makes one adjacent ball enter before the other.
Rollers were removed to save weight and change presentation while retaining the launch height.
A slower powered top wheel was added after South Florida to reduce backspin and bounce-outs.
source_reviews.limitations: Third-regional and Championship states are reported retrospectively. The interview does not quantify the impact of changes or establish full event configurations.

source_reviews.title: 179 2022 reveal discussion
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the announcement and team follow-up text.
facts: The team linked its reveal and acknowledged other teams adapting its climb concept.
source_reviews.limitations: Commenter interpretations of the mechanism are separate from team evidence.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Swamp Thing deliberately brought two neighboring balls to a mouth that narrowed to one. Instead of expecting a symmetric pair to sort itself out, it used a powered contact to move one ahead. The robot then handled wrong-color cargo according to where it sat, with a turret shooter above that path and a separate rotating climber.
piece_flow: The broad foam contacts draw cargo toward the narrow index entrance.
An agitator offsets side-by-side arrivals and the indexer stages them individually. Position and color sensing select forward or rearward clearing according to order.
The indexer delivers to an O-ring main wheel and later powered upper wheel. Hood and flywheel settings establish the shot.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The team kept the indexer tall after observing its shots clear defenders. That decision sets feed length, elevated mass and the path the climber must clear. The climb uses large rotations with a wrist changing the hook orientation relative to the bar. Check the mechanism with the robot swinging and with the wrist at both end poses.

subsystems.name: Foam collector and agitator
subsystems.construction: Foam pickup contacts in round and experimental block forms, with a separate powered rotating contact at the narrow index entry.
subsystems.operation: Acquire across a wide mouth and move one ball ahead when two arrive together.
subsystems.team_rationale: Side pickup was weaker than desired early on. The team found additional foam performed comparably to foam plus mecanum in its tests.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An agitator is useful when it breaks symmetry. Driving both pieces harder into a narrow opening can raise stall load without creating a winner.
subsystems.interfaces: The agitator needs contact before the pair reaches its fully wedged position.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Feed equal and unequal pairs repeatedly. Record which jams clear automatically and how worn foam changes the result.
subsystems.unknowns: Drive and agitator sizes and power are unknown.

subsystems.name: Indexer and rejection
subsystems.construction: Position sensors, added color sensor and a reduced number of transport wheels.
subsystems.operation: Stage pieces and clear the wrong color along the available front or rear path before scoring a correct one.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team removed contacts to reduce mass and alter presentation while preserving shooting height.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Removing rollers works where gravity or adjacent powered contacts still support the ball at the next handoff.
subsystems.interfaces: Wrong-color handling depends on the order and may occupy the path the following ball needs.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test both wrong/correct orders and a partially cleared ball after reversal.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact outlets, sensor locations and flow timing remain open.

subsystems.name: Turret and powered upper contact
subsystems.construction: Yawing turret, O-ring main contact, adjustable hood and a top powered roller added after South Florida.
subsystems.operation: Match hood and wheel settings to shot location and use the slower upper contact to alter release spin.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team observed bounce-outs and wanted to reduce the earlier backspin.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare shots at matched exit trajectory before assigning the improvement to spin alone. The upper contact also affects exit speed and ball support.
subsystems.interfaces: Indexer presentation and both wheel contacts determine compression at launch.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect upper motor retention and test hot restart after successive shots.
subsystems.unknowns: Measured spin and dispersion are unknown.

subsystems.name: Rotating traversal climb
subsystems.construction: Gas-assisted deployment and rotating arms with changing wrist attitude at the hooks.
subsystems.operation: Rotate past each bar, settle onto it, and continue after transferring support.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team reported choosing roughly ten seconds because faster attempts sometimes behaved unpredictably.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A wider capture window can improve expected completion despite a slower peak time.
subsystems.interfaces: The wrist must retain the old rung until the new one can carry load.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure repeatability over approach angle, swing phase and worn hooks.

revisions: Removed planned bump bar, then switched to foam-only contacts before the third regional. Revised indexer and added powered top wheel.
transferable_principles: When a wide intake feeds one slot, make the pair test an explicit acceptance case.
Compare reliable completion time with best-case climb time.
disconfirming_conditions: A dual-lane feed may retain the value of paired pickup if it keeps both balls supported all the way to release.
The raised path pays off only if obstruction avoidance outweighs center-of-mass and service costs.
remaining_gaps: Climb load path, indexer drawing, cycle and jam rates.
recommended_images: Request a top-down image of paired cargo at the agitator and a side view of the two shooter contacts.
